front.title: Temporal Provenance and Reference Profile for QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement

abstract.t: This document specifies the EAP Temporal-Provenance and Reference Profile (EAP-TPRP), an external evidence profile for QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement (EFFECT_ACK) version 1. The profile allows an evaluator to authenticate and compare a source-order marker associated with an immutable source event against the local receipt order of one designated receiver.

EAP-TPRP defines the classification RETROGRADE_REFERENCE for the limited case in which a receiver authenticates a later local receipt that refers to an earlier marker in the same comparable source-order domain. The classification is a statement about two evidence orders. It is not a statement that a signal travelled backward, that a past event changed, that content is true, or that a sender had a particular intent.

The profile is deliberately external to the closed EFFECT_ACK version-1 JSON record. It is bound through the existing evidence-reference and policy mechanisms and does not change any version-1 wire field, state, DONE predicate, authorization rule, or IANA registry.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: An effect-control system often needs more than evidence of receipt. It can also need to determine which authenticated source event an evidence object describes, whether two source-order markers are comparable, and whether locally received evidence arrived in a different order from that source reference.

QIK-VRT EFFECT_ACK version 1 separates transport receipt from authorization for a downstream effect. Its closed record contains generic evidence digests and a policy binding, rather than a field for every possible evidence profile. This document defines one such profile. It is designed so that a deployment can require and validate temporal-provenance evidence without changing the EFFECT_ACK version-1 wire format.

The profile compares two orderings for one comparison: source order and receiver receipt order. A source-order marker is not presumed to be a globally synchronized clock reading. It is an authenticated, deployment-scoped ordering value for a named source-order domain. A receiver receipt sequence is not presumed to establish a universal order among receivers. It is a monotonically increasing local sequence for one receiver identity.

The term RETROGRADE_REFERENCE is intentionally operational. It means only that the relation defined in has been validated. The term neither introduces a new physical theory nor changes the causal direction of a network delivery.

ul.li: Bind a source event, a source-order marker, and the immutable object described by that event to authenticated evidence.
Bind a receiver identity and a locally monotonic receipt sequence to the same evidence comparison.
Define deterministic FORWARD_REFERENCE, RETROGRADE_REFERENCE, and INDETERMINATE classifications.
Permit a deployment policy to require the profile using the existing EFFECT_ACK version-1 evidence and policy bindings.
State security, privacy, retention, and non-claim boundaries explicitly.
This profile does not modify the closed EFFECT_ACK version-1 record.
This profile does not authorize an effect merely because a classification is present.
This profile does not establish the semantic truth, legality, safety, or completeness of a payload or its evidence.
This profile does not provide a global clock, global total order, or synchronization protocol.
This profile does not establish backward signalling, retroactive alteration of an event, superluminal communication, physical or ontic retrocausality, or sender intent.
This profile does not identify a natural person solely from an identifier, key, signature, or receipt record.

section.name: Conventions and Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Architecture and Compatibility
section.t: An EAP-TPRP deployment contains at least a source authority, a receiver, an evidence store or transport, a profile verifier, an EFFECT_ACK evaluator, and an effect executor. The source authority and receiver can be distinct components or may be the same component in a local deployment. Each role MUST be identified in the deployment security profile.

EAP-TPRP is an external evidence profile. The base protocol remains a closed version-1 record with its existing five states and DONE-only ordinary-release rule. A deployment MUST NOT add EAP-TPRP members to a version-1 EFFECT_ACK record. It MUST instead bind the exact profile evidence object through existing evidence_refs, required_evidence_refs, policy_id, policy_version, and policy_hash mechanisms.

A deployment that requires EAP-TPRP for a proposed effect MUST describe that requirement in its immutable policy descriptor. If the required profile evidence is unavailable, malformed, unauthenticated, non-comparable, stale under local policy, or fails rederivation, the evaluator MUST NOT treat the requirement as satisfied. The base protocol's existing state-selection and release rules determine the resulting EFFECT_ACK state.

RETROGRADE_REFERENCE is an evidence classification, not a base-protocol state or decision. A deployment policy MAY treat it as a condition for additional review, isolation, blocking, or continued evaluation. It MUST NOT infer an ordinary release from the classification alone.

section.name: Profile Evidence Object
section.t: A profile evidence object MUST be an I-JSON object encoded as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark. Its canonical representation uses the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) from after Unicode NFC normalization. A digest identifier has the form sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

The profile has version string eap-tprp-1. A missing required member, an unsupported profile version, duplicate normalized member names, a floating-point number, or an integer outside the I-JSON safe-integer range MUST cause profile validation to fail. The deployment MAY carry the object as application/json; this document does not register a media type.

section.t: Optional members MAY carry an RFC 3339 receipt timestamp, local transport context, key-discovery context, retention information, or an application-defined review reason. Optional members MUST be included in the provenance commitment projection unless the deployment profile explicitly lists the member as uncommitted volatile telemetry. A receiver timestamp is not required for the classification and MUST NOT substitute for receipt_sequence.

section.name: Assertion and Commitment Projections
section.t: The source assertion projection is the canonical object containing profile_version, evidence_id, subject_digest, source_order_domain, source_event_id, source_order_marker, and source_principal. The source_assertion_digest MUST equal the SHA-256 digest of that projection.

The receiver observation projection is the canonical object containing profile_version, evidence_id, source_assertion_digest, receiver_id, receipt_sequence, and baseline_evidence_digest. The receiver_assertion_digest MUST equal the SHA-256 digest of that projection.

The provenance commitment projection is the full profile evidence object with provenance_commitment removed. The provenance_commitment MUST equal the SHA-256 digest of that projection. A profile verifier MUST validate all three digest projections before using the evidence object.

The source_authentication_ref MUST resolve, under the deployment security profile, to an authenticated assertion over the source assertion digest by a principal authorized for source_principal and source_order_domain. The receiver_authentication_ref MUST similarly resolve to an authenticated assertion over the receiver assertion digest by a principal authorized for receiver_id. A digest, signature, certificate, or key identifier does not by itself establish the truth of the described payload or the identity of a natural person.

section.name: Reference Classification
section.t: Let b be the validated baseline evidence object and c be the validated current evidence object. The verifier MUST only compare b and c when all of the following conditions are true:

ol.li: b.receipt_sequence is strictly less than c.receipt_sequence;
both source assertions and both receiver observations authenticate successfully under the deployment security profile; and
the baseline digest in c equals the canonical evidence-object digest of b.

section.t: If any condition is false, c.classification MUST be INDETERMINATE. If all conditions are true, the verifier MUST use the following algorithm and MUST reject a producer-supplied classification that differs from its rederived result:

RETROGRADE_REFERENCE therefore means that, for one receiver and one comparable source-order domain, the later local receipt refers to an earlier authenticated source-order marker than the designated baseline. It does not mean that c was received before it was sent, that either source event was changed, or that one event physically caused another event in a reverse direction.

A receiver MUST assign receipt_sequence monotonically for every profile evidence object it emits. It MUST NOT reuse a receipt_sequence for different evidence_id values. A deployment requiring detection of deletion or rewriting MUST retain an authenticated append-only anchor or equivalent independent commitment for its sequence; local monotonicity alone does not detect a complete rewrite by a compromised receiver.

section.name: Profile CDDL
section.t: This section defines the JSON member shape. The authentication, canonicalization, and comparison predicates are specified in the main text.

The open tail in the CDDL permits application-specific optional members. A deployment that requires a closed profile object MUST publish that stricter policy. An optional member MUST NOT alter the classification algorithm unless a future profile version explicitly defines its effect.

section.name: Binding to EFFECT_ACK Version 1
section.t: A base-protocol evaluator that requires this profile MUST place the digest of every required EAP-TPRP evidence object in both evidence_refs and required_evidence_refs of its EFFECT_ACK version-1 record. The policy descriptor identified by policy_id, policy_version, and policy_hash MUST identify the accepted EAP-TPRP version, authentication methods, principal authorization rules, evidence retrieval method, freshness policy, and the required response to each classification.

The base-protocol consumer MUST validate the referenced profile evidence or rely on an authenticated evaluator authorized by the deployment to make that assertion. It MUST still independently apply every base-protocol release condition. EAP-TPRP neither replaces origin_checked, context_checked, semantics_reconstructed, risk_classified, nor any other base-protocol condition.

In particular, a RETROGRADE_REFERENCE classification MUST NOT map directly to EFFECT_ACK_DONE. It MAY cause a policy-specific additional check or state selection, but the policy and base protocol, not this classification alone, control any downstream effect.

section.name: Profile Producer
section.t: A conforming producer MUST create canonical source and receiver assertion projections, bind them to authorized authentication evidence, calculate the digest projections, select the classification according to , and calculate provenance_commitment. It MUST NOT emit FORWARD_REFERENCE or RETROGRADE_REFERENCE without a valid baseline and all required authenticated order comparisons.

section.name: Profile Verifier
section.t: A conforming verifier MUST parse the I-JSON object, validate the CDDL shape and bounds, verify all digest projections, retrieve and validate the source and receiver authentication references, authorize the relevant principals, validate the baseline, rederive classification, and apply local freshness and replay policy. It MUST treat a missing, unauthenticated, malformed, stale, or non-comparable comparison as not satisfying a policy requirement.

section.name: Base-Protocol Deployment
section.t: A base-protocol deployment claiming to require EAP-TPRP MUST bind the profile evidence through the existing version-1 policy and evidence mechanisms. It MUST NOT claim that the profile changes the version-1 wire format. It MUST document the effect of each classification and the fail-closed behavior for unavailable or invalid profile evidence.

section.name: Test Vectors
section.t: The following vectors show the classification relation. Values marked authenticated are fixtures for a verifier whose authentication-profile test double accepts the named principals. They are not cryptographic key material and do not demonstrate a production signature scheme.

tr.td: receiver r, receipt 7, domain d, marker 20
receiver r, receipt 8, domain d, marker 10
receiver r, receipt 7, domain d, marker 10
receiver r, receipt 8, domain d, marker 20
receiver r, receipt 7, domain d1, marker 20
receiver r, receipt 8, domain d2, marker 10
receiver r, receipt 7, domain d, marker 20
receiver r, receipt 8, domain d, marker 10; source assertion fails
receiver r, receipt 7, domain d, marker 20
receiver r, receipt 7, domain d, marker 10

section.t: A machine-readable companion vector set is part of the local staging package. A production conformance suite MUST additionally test duplicate names, canonicalization failures, invalid digests, forged or unauthorized assertions, replay, receipt-sequence reuse, missing baselines, equal source-order markers, stale evidence, and policy binding to the base protocol.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: An attacker can attempt to forge a source-order marker, substitute a baseline, reorder local observations, replay an old valid evidence object, use incomparable domains as if they were comparable, compromise a source or receiver key, or bypass the EFFECT_ACK gate. A profile deployment MUST authenticate both source and receiver assertions and MUST authorize the principals that make them.

Hash identifiers provide content binding under the security assumptions of SHA-256. They do not authenticate a principal, establish freshness, demonstrate source honesty, or prevent a complete rewrite of an unanchored evidence history. Deployments requiring rewrite detection MUST retain an authenticated independent anchor. Deployments SHOULD bind profile assertions to an authenticated session or trusted evidence store to resist substitution and replay.

Source-order markers can be abused when a source authority is compromised or has an ambiguous domain definition. A deployment MUST define who can authorize a source-order domain, how source-order markers are generated, and whether markers are strictly monotonic, merely monotonic, or allocated in ranges. A verifier MUST NOT compare markers from different domains or from unauthenticated domain authorities.

RETROGRADE_REFERENCE can be used as a forensic or review signal. It MUST NOT be treated as evidence of malicious intent, deception, causal influence, or a physical anomaly without additional policy-defined evidence. A correct classification only verifies the bound order relation under the stated authentication and retention assumptions.

Profile validation and evidence retrieval can create denial-of-service opportunities. Implementations MUST bound object size, identifier size, recursion, signature-validation work, baseline retrieval, cache growth, and the number of candidate baselines. Failure to complete validation within a policy-defined budget MUST fail the profile requirement rather than permit an effect.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Source and receiver identifiers, receipt sequences, timestamps, source-event identifiers, and evidence references can disclose system topology, user behavior, commercial activity, location, or sensitive decision timing. A cryptographic identifier is not anonymization, and a digest can reveal low-entropy data through guessing.

Deployments SHOULD use scoped pseudonymous identifiers, access-controlled evidence stores, data minimization, retention limits, and access logging. They SHOULD avoid placing personal data in source_event_id, evidence_id, or optional reason fields. A deployment MUST document who can retrieve evidence, how a subject can request redaction where applicable, and how a redaction preserves the fact that a verification limitation now exists.

Receipt sequences may enable correlation across contexts. Deployments SHOULD scope receiver_id and receipt_sequence to the smallest domain needed for the stated effect-control purpose. They MUST NOT publish a global receipt history merely because the profile can represent one.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests no IANA actions. EAP-TPRP is an external evidence profile carried through existing EFFECT_ACK version-1 evidence references. It defines no new base-protocol wire version, state, media type, registry, or protocol number.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section is non-normative.

At the time this local candidate was prepared, the profile has a machine-readable classification-vector set and a small local verifier. It has not been submitted to the IETF Datatracker, has no IETF consensus or endorsement, and has not been shown interoperable between independently developed implementations. The base protocol's public individual Internet-Draft status does not confer a standard status on this companion candidate.
